The story follows a clear and logical progression where the beginning, middle, and end are tightly interwoven. The initial mystery of Daniel's recurring dream about an unlived-in apartment with his ex-wife, Rachel, sets up the central emotional tension between his past and his current life with Isabel. In the middle, the discovery of the forgotten keys acts as a catalyst, unlocking a repressed, joyful memory of looking at that apartment and subsequently going canoeing with Rachel. This seamlessly leads to the resolution, where the canoeing motif bridges his past and present: Daniel and Isabel go canoeing together, allowing him to integrate his past memories without letting them rival his current relationship. Every scene, piece of dialogue, and symbol (the apartment, the keys, the canoe paddle, the reeds) serves the overarching theme of reconciling the past with the present, creating a harmonious and satisfying whole.
